why: Most recent dated official statement (14 July 2026) naming NDS2, the Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan, the National ICT Policy and the National AI Strategy 2026-2030 as the current frameworks driving Zimbabwe's digital transformation agenda; the primary 2022-2027 ICT Policy full text and the Smart Zimbabwe Master Plan are already held in raw/ (DUP-EXACT), so this dated confirmation is the instrument's current-standing evidence.

Most significant in-window event: official launch of National Development Strategy 2 (2026-2030), the successor national plan whose objectives include a knowledge-driven and digitally enabled economy.

Distinct second event: launch of the AI for Impact Challenge and finalisation of the National AI Charter and AI Strategy Implementation Office, moving the digital-transformation agenda from policy to delivery.

Clearest available record that a customised government enterprise-architecture framework and implementation roadmap for Zimbabwe was completed (project ran September 2023-September 2024) -- the instrument's current standing, absent a standalone published Zimbabwean interoperability-framework document.

Most significant in-window event: official handover of the Enterprise Architecture Model blueprint, with the Minister announcing a planned Government Service Bus for cross-ministry data sharing under 'radical interoperability'.
Distinct second event: launch of the National Migration Data Strategy 2025-2030, a sector data-sharing framework coordinated by ZIMSTAT, Immigration and IOM.

POTRAZ's implementation guidelines (CDPG series, 2025), whose CDPG 4 clause 4.6(f) requires highly sensitive systems such as core-banking platforms and critical financial systems to be hosted locally in Zimbabwe absent prior written approval -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: POTRAZ's Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 moves data-protection compliance, including cross-border/localisation obligations, from voluntary licensing to mandatory risk-based inspections from 1 September 2026.
Distinct second event: POTRAZ's 8 March 2026 notice demanding immediate licensing regularisation, a year after the original March 2025 deadline.

No standalone national open-data policy was found; this is the most authoritative dated primary evidence of what currently exists in practice -- ZIMSTAT's Open Data Portal 2.0 and SDMX rollout, the operational open-data instrument closest to the indicator.

The principal cybersecurity/data-protection statute, Act No. 5 of 2021, establishing a Cyber Security Centre and Data Protection Authority and amending the Criminal Law Code with cybercrime offences -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: Ministry of ICT announced completion of the National Cybersecurity Strategy, an overarching policy framework for institutional structures, capacity building and cooperation.

Distinct second event: POTRAZ's 24 January 2026 statement clarifying that Zimbabwe has no standalone Cyber Crimes Act, with cybercrime offences governed by Part VIII of the Criminal Law (Codification and Reform) Act.

No standalone digital-ID/e-ID Act was found; this is the core national-registration statute (commenced 1976, consolidated to 31 December 2016) authorising the identity register, fingerprint/photograph capture and identity-document issuance underlying Zimbabwe's civil-registration and e-passport rollout -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: enacted Act No. 6 of 2026 inserts new constitutional section 43A assigning the Registrar-General responsibility for voter registration and custody of voters' rolls, consolidating identity-register control.

Distinct second event: commissioning of the Mutare Provincial Registry Office for biometric e-passport and national-ID services, described by the Registrar-General as foundational to a digital identity system.

The foundational statute (Act 21 of 2001, commenced 16 November 2001) for recognition, operation, regulation and supervision of Zimbabwe's payment-clearing and settlement systems, including electronic payment instructions -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: Statutory Instrument 65 of 2026 creates a regulatory fintech sandbox at the Victoria Falls International Financial Services Centre, with an express licensing track for low-risk payment solutions and open-banking API interoperability requirements.

Reused from gov.legislate--cybersecurity-legislation: the Cyber and Data Protection Act's transborder-flow and inter-related-processing provisions are the strongest enacted instrument bearing on lawful data linking and sharing; no dedicated interoperability-enabling Act was found.

Most significant in-window event found: MOHCC's draft Zimbabwe Core FHIR Implementation Guide (v0.1.0), the national technical standard defining how health-information systems structure, exchange and interpret data -- a concrete interoperability-enablement instrument.
The controlling statute (Act 1 of 2007, commenced 1 July 2009) establishing the Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (ZIMSTAT) and its census/survey/data-collection powers -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: on World Statistics Day, ZIMSTAT publicly stated the Census and Statistics Act is outdated and does not adequately support administrative-data sharing, putting legislative reform on the institutional agenda.
Distinct second event: ZIMSTAT adopted a formal Board Charter defining the statutory Board's governance framework, roles and ethical standards.

The controlling statute (Act No. 1 of 2020, Chapter 10:33), published and commenced 1 July 2020, implementing constitutional section 62 access-to-information rights and repealing AIPPA -- the instrument itself.

Most significant in-window event: High Court judgment (handed down 24 December 2025) holding that withholding the Uchena Commission report violates constitutional section 62(1) access rights and ordering its publication within 90 days.
Distinct second event: High Court ruling clarifying that Banking Act section 76 banking-secrecy provisions can lawfully restrict the constitutional access-to-information right.

Zimbabwe's own enacted transborder-data-flow and cross-border-cooperation instrument (Part VII, ss.28-29); the AU Malabo Convention's own status table shows no Zimbabwean signature or ratification, so this domestic Act is the most authoritative document on Zimbabwe's regional legal-harmonisation position.

SADC's own account of the 26 June 2026 Bulawayo Cluster Meeting of Ministers (hosted by Zimbabwe) reaffirming implementation of the SADC Digital Transformation Strategy and regional ICT/infrastructure integration frameworks.

Zimbabwe's President was elected COMESA Vice-Chairperson at the 9 October 2025 summit, whose adopted communique urges Member States to adopt digitalised trade-facilitation instruments and advance the COMESA Digital Retail Payment Platform -- a distinct regional-integration event from the June 2026 SADC ministerial meeting.

COMESA's own current statement (updated to April 2026) that Zimbabwe is one of five Member States implementing the COMESA Electronic Certificate of Origin and one of fifteen on the Electronic Single Window, the clearest primary evidence of Zimbabwe's participation in shared regional digital trade infrastructure.

The operator's own announcement that the Plumtree-Bulawayo phase of the Powertel/Paratus Botswana-Zimbabwe-Zambia cross-border fibre corridor is live, carrying 800Gbps of equipped capacity -- a distinct, dated infrastructure-commissioning event separate from the June 2026 SADC ministerial meeting.

SADC's own account of the 26 June 2026 Bulawayo Cluster Meeting of Ministers (hosted by Zimbabwe) reaffirming implementation of the SADC Digital Transformation Strategy and regional ICT/infrastructure integration frameworks.

Reports POTRAZ's SADC nomination to lead regional data-protection capacity building in 2026 and states that 24 cross-border personal-data transfers had been authorised by POTRAZ under the Cyber and Data Protection Act by late 2025, a dated operational figure distinct from the customs-data event below.
